chunks: What the Shaykh—may Allah Most High support him—informed me of, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd al-Madāʾinī, from Muṣaddiq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī, who said:

Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام was asked about a menstruating woman who perspires in a garment she wears. He said: “There is nothing upon her, unless something from her fluid or some other filth reaches it; then she should wash that specific spot which was affected.”

key_terms.الْمَوْضِعَ: the specific place or spot affected
key_terms.ثَوْبٍ: a garment or piece of clothing
key_terms.مَائِهَا: her fluid, referring here to menstrual discharge

ai.seo_question: Does the sweat of a menstruating woman make her clothes impure?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the garment worn by a menstruating woman. It states that mere perspiration does not make the garment impure; only direct contact with her fluid or another impurity requires washing the exact affected area.
